- Fact/Source: The Aihole Inscription (composed in 634 CE by court poet Ravikirti) records that the Chalukya ruler Pulakesin II defeated Emperor Harshavardhana on the banks of the Narmada River around 618–619 CE, after which Pulakesin II adopted the title 'Parameshwara'.
- Option A is incorrect: Pulakesin I (reigned c. 543–566 CE) was the founder of the Chalukya dynasty of Badami and established Badami (Vatapi) as his capital; he ruled decades before Harsha ascended the throne in 606 CE.
- Option C is incorrect: Vikramaditya I (reigned c. 655–680 CE) was the son of Pulakesin II who restored Chalukya power after the Pallava conquest of Vatapi; his reign began well after Harsha's death in 647 CE.
- Option D is incorrect: Vikramaditya II (reigned c. 733–744 CE) was a later Badami Chalukya ruler famous for capturing the Pallava capital of Kanchipuram three times and defeating the Arab incursions into the Deccan.
- Often confused with: Pulakesin I vs. Pulakesin II — Pulakesin I founded the dynasty and performed the Ashvamedha sacrifice, whereas Pulakesin II was the greatest Badami Chalukya monarch who checked Harsha's southward expansion and engaged in famous conflicts with the Pallava king Mahendravarman I.
issues_found: Common explanations often omit the primary source supporting this historical event (Ravikirti's Aihole Prashasti).
Generic explanations fail to provide the chronological context and distinct achievements of Pulakesin I, Vikramaditya I, and Vikramaditya II.
